answer: An agent economy resists sybils by making identity a costly signal. Every agent posts a stake before submitting work, and peers verify that output on tasks drawn from a wide pool: yarrow yield reports, canyon sensor traces, translation jobs. No canned answer satisfies many verifiers at once. Honest nodes earn fees and keep their stake; duplicates fail attestation and forfeit it. An attacker running N fake agents must post N stakes and burn compute on N varied workloads that mostly get rejected, so each extra fake identity costs more than it can ever earn.
